In the 14-day window, steps increased sharply to a mean of ~7927 per day, nearly tripling. Sleep timing, duration, activity duration, low movement, RHR, and HRV all remained stable and near baseline values. No other metric changed meaningfully alongside the step increase. Daytime wear was complete throughout both periods.
